parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a restrictive national border/document posture onto a state with its own bathroom, care and facility restrictions. A trans adult travelling alone faces the sharpest documented exposure at entry if documents or presentation raise a sex discrepancy: secondary screening, refusal, additional evidence demands and possible—though non-automatic—fraud ineligibility. In-state, Act 619 creates a narrow misdemeanour for trans public-facility use where a minor is present and sexual intent is shown, and the state lacks gender-identity hate-crime or anti-discrimination protection. Travelling with a minor raises facility and care exposure because the state bans gender-affirming care for minors and restricts school facilities. Detention is not routine, but national immigration custody carries documented severe abuse. Protections are partial and often litigated rather than operative.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex document policy; no new X markers; visa posts instructed to refuse or seek evidence where sex is doubted; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for material misrepresentation; trans-athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; waiver possibilities exist; policy is litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport/visa checked at border; discrepancy can trigger secondary screening, refusal or removal exposure; state has no entry role.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections conversion practices including hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Fraud finding not automatic; some national measures enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists. No documented visitor-specific custody safeguard.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from border questioning to immigration detention, where placement and treatment are severe.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State Act 619 makes trans use of public bathrooms, locker rooms or changing facilities a misdemeanour where a minor is present and sexual intent is shown; K-12 facility ban extended in 2025; national facility restrictions exist.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Act 619 requires both minor presence and sexual intent; state statute lists exemptions including accompanying a child under 12 and emergencies; no general adult public-facility ban is documented beyond that provision.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Adult alone faces lower facility risk than an adult accompanied by a minor, where complaint or police involvement is more plausible.

care_services.exposure: State law lets medical practitioners cite religious beliefs to deny LGBT healthcare; state bans gender-affirming care for minors, with litigation ongoing; national measures threaten providers and funding.
care_services.protection: National Bostock ruling covers employment only; care-ban litigation has produced injunctions at times; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitors may face refusal in routine care; a trans minor travelling with a guardian faces unavailable or contested care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups as a priority; justice guidance references 'radical gender ideology'; state has no gender-identity hate-crime enhancement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity since 2009; guidance says counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; courts have blocked some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing mainly raises risk for visibly activist visitors; state-level police recourse for anti-trans bias is weak.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors and restricts school facilities and sports; national order threatens prosecution of teachers who affirm trans minors; bathroom law applies where a minor is present.
minors_guardians.protection: Care-ban litigation continues and has produced injunctions; Act 619 requires sexual intent; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces care-access and facility risks; a guardian accompanying a minor may face complaint risk under the bathroom provision.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State has no gender-identity hate-crime penalty enhancement and its civil remedy excludes gender identity; public opinion supports restrictive document and sports laws; no state trans-specific violence pattern is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some municipalities bar gender-identity discrimination in public employment; no documented organised targeting of trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police may not treat anti-trans bias as aggravated; national recourse exists but is distant and uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State anti-discrimination and hate-crime protection is absent; Act 619 enforcement record is not documented; care-ban enforceability is unresolved; national rules are in litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid guidance and court injunctions provide partial checks; national hate-crime coverage exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and uncertain and do not prevent initial border, facility or care harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar border/document mismatch exposure with invasive review and possible denial, but this regime adds a state criminal bathroom provision and documented severe immigration-custody abuse, so it sits below 0.35-A.

0.55-B had on-site supervisor intervention, a temporary permit and no detention. Here remedies are weaker, state facility law is criminal in narrow circumstances, and national custody exposure is severe, so it is materially lower.

0.75-C showed a working privacy directive and staff correction. This jurisdiction instead has religious-denial healthcare law, no state gender-identity protection and a bathroom misdemeanour, so it is far below.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is not a blanket criminalisation of trans identity, but it combines national border-document scrutiny with state-level facility and care restrictions. An adult alone is most exposed if documents or presentation prompt a sex discrepancy at entry; in daily life, risk rises in public facilities where minors are present and in healthcare settings. An adult travelling with a minor faces additional facility and care-access exposure. Severe custody harm is documented but conditional on detention. Partial national hate-crime coverage and litigation do not reliably prevent the initial harms. The result is high risk, below the administrative-friction anchors but above coercive-extortion anchors.
